1	// Package agentusageview is the `:agent-usage` screen: the Claude Code
2	// sessions found on this machine.
3	//
4	// It reads transcripts' working directory and date only, never their content
5	// (internal/agentusage owns that guarantee).
6	package agentusageview
7	
8	import (
9		"github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles/spinner"
10		tea "github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea"
11	
12		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/agentusage"
13		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/agentusage/pricing"
14		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/config"
15		sharedcomponents "github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/components"
16		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/datatable"
17		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/theme"
18	)
19	
20	// sessionRow is one table row. project is computed once, in Update, so a Cell
21	// never touches the file system or the environment.
22	type sessionRow struct {
23		agentusage.Session
24		project string // theme.FoldHome(Project), or "-" when unknown
25	}
26	
27	// sessionListLoadedMsg carries one listing. gen drops an answer to a read that
28	// a newer one has superseded.
29	type sessionListLoadedMsg struct {
30		gen     int
31		root    string
32		listing agentusage.Listing
33		err     error
34	}
35	
36	// level is the screen on view: the sessions, or the agents of one session.
37	type level int
38	
39	const (
40		levelSessions level = iota
41		levelAgents
42	)
43	
44	// Model is the agent usage view.
45	type Model struct {
46		table   datatable.Model[sessionRow]
47		spinner spinner.Model
48		footer  sharedcomponents.FooterMessage
49	
50		// level says which table is on screen. The sessions table keeps its cursor
51		// and filter while the agents level is open.
52		level level
53		// agentTable lists the agents of open.
54		agentTable datatable.Model[agentRow]
55		// prices is the context's price table, read once in New: ctrl+r keeps it.
56		prices pricing.Table
57		// cost is the cost picture of usage, recomputed by every withRows.
58		cost pricing.Summary
59		open agentusage.Session
60		// usage is the last parse of open, kept for what the footer says about it.
61		usage agentusage.Usage
62		// agentGen numbers the parses, as gen numbers the listings.
63		agentGen int
64		// agg reads the open session incrementally. Update owns it; a Cmd only
65		// ever gets a copy of its Cursor (Rule 110). nil at the sessions level.
66		agg *agentusage.Aggregate
67		// reading is true while a read of agentGen is in flight: one at a time.
68		reading bool
69		// fullPending records a ctrl+r pressed during a read; the full read starts
70		// when that read answers.
71		fullPending bool
72		// pollStopped says the poll chain ended (settled session, deleted
73		// transcript): a late tick of the same generation starts nothing. A full
74		// read clears it.
75		pollStopped bool
76		// agentsLoading says a full read is in flight (the footer spinner).
77		agentsLoading bool
78		// agentsErr says the most recent parse failed (a state, like loadErr).
79		agentsErr bool
80		// clock is what the agent states are computed against; written in Update only.
81		clock statusClock
82		// width and height are the last viewport size, for both tables.
83		width, height int
84	
85		// gen numbers the reads; only the answer to the latest one is kept.
86		gen     int
87		loading bool
88		// loadErr says the most recent read failed. It is a state rather than a
89		// timed message so the empty-listing sentence cannot take its place.
90		loadErr bool
91		// root is the projects directory the last successful read listed.
92		root    string
93		omitted int
94	}
95	
96	// New builds the view with its first read pending.
97	func New(cfg *config.Config) Model {
98		sp := spinner.New()
99		sp.Spinner = spinner.Dot
100		sp.Style = theme.SpinnerStyle()
101	
102		return Model{
103			loading: true,
104			prices:  pricesFrom(cfg),
105			spinner: sp,
106			table: datatable.New(datatable.Config[sessionRow]{
107				Columns: sessionColumns(),
108				// The listing arrives newest first, which is the order wanted.
109				SortColumn: -1,
110			}),
111			agentTable: datatable.New(datatable.Config[agentRow]{
112				Columns: agentColumns(),
113				// Opens as the tree (orchestrator, then sub-agents); `.` sorts by Total.
114				SortColumn: -1,
115			}),
116		}
117	}
118	
119	// Init starts the first read and the spinner.
120	func (m Model) Init() tea.Cmd {
121		cmds := []tea.Cmd{listSessionsCmd(m.gen), m.spinner.Tick}
122		if m.level == levelAgents {
123			// Init cannot change the model: Update restarts the open session's chain.
124			cmds = append(cmds, resumeCmd())
125		}
126		return tea.Batch(cmds...)
127	}

7	)

9	// The reasons, written once so the header, the footer and the tests cannot
10	// drift apart on the wording (Rule 129 — English US).
11	const (
12		reasonNoSession     = "No session to open"
13		reasonInsideSession = "Already inside a session"
14		reasonTopLevel      = "Already at the session list"
15	)
16	
17	// actions is what the keys allow right now, computed once and read by both
18	// halves of the view: GetShortcuts to grey out, the handlers to refuse
19	// (Rule 130).
20	type actions struct {
21		Open  shortcut.Availability // → and enter
22		Close shortcut.Availability // ← and esc
23	}

25	// availability computes the answers from the level and the selected row.
26	func (m Model) availability() actions {
27		var a actions
28		if m.level == levelAgents {
29			a.Open = shortcut.Unavailable(reasonInsideSession)
30			return a
31		}
32		a.Close = shortcut.Unavailable(reasonTopLevel)
33		if _, ok := m.table.Selected(); !ok {
34			a.Open = shortcut.Unavailable(reasonNoSession)
35		}

40	// reason as a Warn: nothing failed, the action does not apply (Rule 128).
41	func (m Model) guard(a shortcut.Availability, act func() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd)) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
42		if !a.Enabled() {
43			return m, m.footer.Warn(a.Reason)

1	package agentusageview
2	
3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"slices"
6		"strings"
7	
8		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/agentusage"
9	)
10	
11	// mainKey is the key of the orchestrator, of which a session has one.
12	const mainKey = "main"
13	
14	// agentKeys names agents so the same one keeps its key from one rebuild to the
15	// next: "main" for the orchestrator, "sub:<ID>#n" for a sub-agent, n counting
16	// the earlier agents that share its ID (an ID is not guaranteed unique). It
17	// must be given the canonical order (agentRows), never the sorted or filtered
18	// one: under a sort, two twins would trade keys whenever they trade ranks.
19	func agentKeys(agents []agentusage.Agent) []string {
20		seen := make(map[string]int, len(agents))
21		keys := make([]string, len(agents))
22		for i, a := range agents {
23			if a.Main {
24				keys[i] = mainKey
25				continue
26			}
27			keys[i] = fmt.Sprintf("sub:%s#%d", a.ID, seen[a.ID])
28			seen[a.ID]++
29		}
30		return keys
31	}
32	
33	// populationOf lists what makes a table "another population" for the column
34	// widths: which agents it holds, and the models each one names. Counts change
35	// on every delta and do not count. A type can change too (its meta arrives
36	// after the transcript) but stays out on purpose: the column is remeasured at
37	// the next ctrl+r or change of population.
38	func populationOf(rows []agentRow) []string {
39		out := make([]string, len(rows))
40		for i, r := range rows {
41			out[i] = r.key + "|" + strings.Join(r.Models, ",")
42		}
43		return out
44	}
45	
46	// withUsage shows u in the agents table, keeping the cursor on the agent it was
47	// on (whatever the filter and the sort do to the order), and clears the
48	// loading and error states. The columns are remeasured only on a full read or
49	// when the population changed, so a two-second delta never reshuffles them.
50	func (m Model) withUsage(u agentusage.Usage, full bool) Model {
51		m = m.withRows(u, full)
52		m.agentsLoading, m.agentsErr = false, false
53		return m
54	}
55	
56	// withRows rebuilds the agents table from u without touching the loading and
57	// error states, so a red footer survives the rebuild.
58	func (m Model) withRows(u agentusage.Usage, full bool) Model {
59		before := populationOf(m.agentTable.Items())
60		selected, hadSelection := m.selectedAgentKey()
61		cursor := m.agentTable.Cursor()
62	
63		rows := agentRows(u, m.agentsTree(), m.clock, m.prices)
64		m.usage = u
65		m.cost = m.prices.Session(u)
66		m.agentTable.SetItems(rows)
67	
68		if full || !slices.Equal(before, populationOf(rows)) {
69			m.agentTable.Remeasure()
70		}
71		m.agentTable.SetCursor(cursor) // clamps when the agent vanished
72		if hadSelection {
73			m.selectAgentKey(selected)
74		}
75		return m
76	}
77	
78	// selectAgentKey moves the cursor onto the visible row with that key, if any.
79	func (m *Model) selectAgentKey(key string) {
80		if i := slices.IndexFunc(m.agentTable.Visible(), func(r agentRow) bool { return r.key == key }); i >= 0 {
81			m.agentTable.SetCursor(i)
82		}
83	}
84	
85	// selectedAgentKey is the key of the row under the cursor.
86	func (m Model) selectedAgentKey() (string, bool) {
87		r, ok := m.agentTable.Selected()
88		return r.key, ok
89	}

1	package agentusage
2	
3	import "time"
4	
5	// Agent is the usage of one agent of a session: the orchestrator (Main) or a
6	// sub-agent.
7	type Agent struct {
8		ID              string
9		Main            bool
10		Type            string // sub-agent type from its meta file; "" if unknown
11		Models          []string
12		Tokens          Tokens
13		ByModel         []ModelUsage // per-model split of Tokens; the "" bucket (no model, or past maxModelsPerAgent) last
14		Messages        int          // distinct message ids
15		PartialMessages int          // messages whose last line has no stop reason
16		State           State
17		SpawnDepth      int
18		ToolCalls       int       // distinct tool_use blocks of the agent's assistant lines
19		FirstActivity   time.Time // earliest line timestamp (UTC); zero if none
20		LastActivity    time.Time // latest line timestamp (UTC); zero if none
21		// key is the table's identity for the agent's lines (the rank of its
22		// transcript); empty means ID. finish clears it from its output.
23		key string
24	}
25	
26	// ModelUsage is the part of an agent's tokens billed to one model, with the
27	// share of its cache writes that used the 1 h cache. Summed over an agent's
28	// ByModel it equals Agent.Tokens.
29	type ModelUsage struct {
30		Model        string // "" for messages that name no model, and for models past maxModelsPerAgent
31		Tokens       Tokens
32		CacheWrite1h int64 // of Tokens.CacheWrite, written with the 1 h cache
33	}
34	
35	// CacheWrite5m is the cache writes that used the 5 min cache.
36	func (m ModelUsage) CacheWrite5m() int64 { return m.Tokens.CacheWrite - m.CacheWrite1h }
37	
38	// Duration is LastActivity - FirstActivity, or 0 unless both are known.
39	func (a Agent) Duration() time.Duration {
40		if a.FirstActivity.IsZero() || a.LastActivity.IsZero() {
41			return 0
42		}
43		return a.LastActivity.Sub(a.FirstActivity)
44	}
45	
46	// PartialOutput reports whether some message of the agent was still being
47	// written (no stop reason on its last line), so its output count is a floor.
48	func (a Agent) PartialOutput() bool { return a.PartialMessages > 0 }
49	
50	// IssueKind classifies a line that could not be counted.
51	type IssueKind int
52	
53	const (
54		IssueUnreadable IssueKind = iota // not JSON, truncated, or bad counters
55		IssueOversized                   // longer than MaxLineBytes
56		IssueOpenFailed                  // a sub-agent transcript could not be opened
57		IssueReadError                   // reading stopped on an I/O error at Offset
58	)
59	
60	// FileIssue locates one skipped line. File is a base name, never a path.
61	type FileIssue struct {
62		File   string
63		Offset int64
64		Kind   IssueKind
65	}
66	
67	// Diagnostics counts what parsing skipped or had to guess.
68	type Diagnostics struct {
69		UnreadableLines     int
70		OversizedLines      int
71		NoUsage             int
72		NoMessageID         int
73		CrossFileDuplicates int
74		MetaMissing         int
75		MetaUnreadable      int
76		TruncatedFiles      []string
77		Files               []FileIssue
78	}
79	
80	// Degraded reports whether anything was skipped or guessed.
81	func (d Diagnostics) Degraded() bool {
82		return d.UnreadableLines > 0 || d.OversizedLines > 0 || d.NoUsage > 0 ||
83			d.NoMessageID > 0 || d.CrossFileDuplicates > 0 || d.MetaMissing > 0 ||
84			d.MetaUnreadable > 0 || len(d.TruncatedFiles) > 0 || len(d.Files) > 0
85	}
86	
87	// Usage is the parsed usage of one session.
88	type Usage struct {
89		SessionID   string
90		Agents      []Agent
91		Versions    []string
92		Diagnostics Diagnostics
93		Billed      Billed
94	}
95	
96	// Billed is the session cost Claude Code recorded itself, in the last
97	// cost-state line of the parent transcript.
98	type Billed struct {
99		USD float64 // 0 unless Known
100		// Known is false while the session runs (no cost-state yet), when any line
101		// follows the last cost-state (the session was resumed), or when that line
102		// is invalid or names another session.
103		Known bool
104	}
105	
106	// Total returns the tokens of every agent.
107	func (u Usage) Total() Tokens {
108		var t Tokens
109		for _, a := range u.Agents {
110			t = t.Add(a.Tokens)
111		}
112		return t
113	}

162	### Per-model tokens (DEVDESK-47)
163	
164	`Agent.ByModel` splits `Agent.Tokens` by model, in first-appearance order, with
165	the bucket of `Model == ""` last. That bucket holds messages that name no model
166	and the models past the cap of 64 per agent (`maxModelsPerAgent`, the cap that
167	already applies to `Models`). The sum of `ByModel` is `Agent.Tokens`, also past
168	the cap and for the lines that spill (`modelTally`, in `limits.go`).
169	
170	Each usage line may carry `usage.cache_creation.ephemeral_1h_input_tokens`: the
171	part of `cache_creation_input_tokens` written with the 1 h cache, which is
172	priced differently from the 5 min one. It is decoded apart, so a value of
173	another shape costs the split and nothing else: an absent, negative,
174	fractional, text or null value is 0, the line stays a usage line, and the token
175	totals do not move. A value above the total is clamped to the total. As for the
176	other counters, the last line of a message wins. `ModelUsage.CacheWrite5m()` is
177	`Tokens.CacheWrite - CacheWrite1h`. Checked on 49 real parent transcripts: the
178	field is on every usage line, 5 min + 1 h equals the total write on all of
179	them, and 1 h writes are 47 % of the cache written. Pricing every write at one
180	rate would be wrong by a large factor, which is why the split exists.
181	
182	### `cost-state` and `Billed` (DEVDESK-47)
183	
184	Claude Code appends a line of root `type` `cost-state` when a session closes. It
185	has no `message` and no `timestamp`; the package reads three keys of it, and no
186	others: `type`, `sessionId`, `totalCostUSD`. It is a `kindCostState` line
187	(`record.go`): it counts for nothing else (no tokens, no version, no activity).
188	
189	`Usage.Billed` is `Billed{USD, Known}`. `Known` is true only when all of these
190	hold:
191	
192	- the cost-state line with the greatest position **in the parent transcript** is
193	  also the parent's last complete line (`parentEnd`, the greatest position of
194	  any complete parent line, readable or not, oversized included);
195	- its `totalCostUSD` is a finite number >= 0;
196	- its `sessionId` equals the session's, or is absent or null (any other value
197	  matches no session).
198	
199	A cost-state line in a sub-agent file is ignored. Both positions are maxima, so
200	a merge is commutative and the incremental result still equals `ParseSession`
201	(see "Incremental reading"). `table.hasLines()` counts the cost-state, so the
202	delta that brings it is not `Empty()` and the view rebuilds; as a consequence a
203	cost-state counts as file activity for `Activity.LastChange`, and updates pause
204	up to 5 min later than before.
205	
206	What 46 of 49 real parents here show (one client version line, 2.1.28x to
207	2.1.30x): the line is always last in the file; a session resumed and closed again
208	appends a new **cumulative** cost-state (7.08 then 12.61 in one file), so the
209	last one is the bill. This is observed, not documented by Claude Code.
210	
211	**Known limit, declared.** Billed goes stale after a line that carries no
212	timestamp and no usage (the delta has no activity to move the view), because the
213	view only rebuilds on a non-empty delta that changes something. It is corrected
214	by the next line with a timestamp, or by `ctrl+r`. The test file states it.
215	
216	The fixture `testdata/v2.1.302-cost/` holds a parent with two models, a 5 min /
217	1 h split, a first cost-state (7.08), more usage, then a second cumulative one
218	(12.61) as the last line; and a sub-agent file with its own cost-state (99,
219	ignored).
220	
221	## Tolerance
222	
223	The format is not a documented API, so the parser degrades rather than fails.

priced differently from the 5 min one. It is decoded apart, so a value of
another shape costs the split and nothing else: an absent, negative,
fractional, text or null value is 0, the line stays a usage line, and the token
totals do not move. A value above the total is clamped to the total. As for the
other counters, the last line of a message wins. `ModelUsage.CacheWrite5m()` is

field is on every usage line, 5 min + 1 h equals the total write on all of
them, and 1 h writes are 47 % of the cache written. Pricing every write at one
rate would be wrong by a large factor, which is why the split exists.

### `cost-state` and `Billed` (DEVDESK-47)

Claude Code appends a line of root `type` `cost-state` when a session closes. It
has no `message` and no `timestamp`; the package reads three keys of it, and no
others: `type`, `sessionId`, `totalCostUSD`. It is a `kindCostState` line
(`record.go`): it counts for nothing else (no tokens, no version, no activity).

`Usage.Billed` is `Billed{USD, Known}`. `Known` is true only when all of these
hold:

- the cost-state line with the greatest position **in the parent transcript** is
  also the parent's last complete line (`parentEnd`, the greatest position of
  any complete parent line, readable or not, oversized included);
- its `totalCostUSD` is a finite number >= 0;
- its `sessionId` equals the session's, or is absent or null (any other value
  matches no session).

A cost-state line in a sub-agent file is ignored. Both positions are maxima, so
a merge is commutative and the incremental result still equals `ParseSession`
(see "Incremental reading"). `table.hasLines()` counts the cost-state, so the
delta that brings it is not `Empty()` and the view rebuilds; as a consequence a
cost-state counts as file activity for `Activity.LastChange`, and updates pause
up to 5 min later than before.

What 46 of 49 real parents here show (one client version line, 2.1.28x to
2.1.30x): the line is always last in the file; a session resumed and closed again
appends a new **cumulative** cost-state (7.08 then 12.61 in one file), so the

timestamp and no usage (the delta has no activity to move the view), because the

583	## The `:agent-usage` view
584	
585	`internal/ui/agentusageview`, opened with `:agent-usage` or `:au`. It lists the
586	Claude Code sessions found on this machine, newest first, and reads only where
587	and when a session ran at this level (see the privacy amendment above). `→` or
588	`enter` opens the selected session's agents (DEVDESK-42, below).
589	
590	| Column | Content |
591	|---|---|
592	| Project | the `cwd`, **full path** with home folded to `~` (`theme.FoldHome`, done once per row in `Update`, never in a `Cell`). Cut from the left when too narrow, so the leaf stays visible. `-` (dim) when the transcript named none. |
593	| Last active | the transcript's `ModTime`, local time, `2006-01-02 15:04` |
594	| Session | the first 8 characters of the ID. `Optional`: the first column dropped on a narrow terminal. The filter (`/`) matches the full ID. |
595	
596	- **Rule 139.** The body is always `m.table.View()`. Loading, an empty
597	  machine and a filter with no match all leave a table with its header.
598	- **Header** (`GetHeaderInfo`): `Sessions` (rows visible after the filter) and,
599	  only when non-zero, `Skipped` (`Listing.Omitted`).
600	- **Footer** (Rule 128), derived on every frame with no timer, in this order:
601	  a failed read (red, "Failed to list Claude Code sessions — check logs"; the
602	  error is logged, never shown, since it can name a path), then loading (spinner,
603	  "Reading Claude Code sessions..."), then "No Claude Code sessions found in
604	  <root>" when the listing is empty before any filter.
605	- **Shortcuts**: `ctrl+r` Refresh, `/` Filter, `?` Help. The same keys in every
606	  state, none greyed (Rule 130): each always acts. `.` cycles the sort column
607	  and is listed in `?` only (Rule 138).
608	- **Reload on every entry.** The view is built once and stays cached in the
609	  router (`createView` stops if it already exists). The reload comes from
610	  `switchView` (`internal/app/command_line.go`), which calls `Init()` on every
611	  entry, and `Init` starts a read. The rows from the previous visit stay on
612	  screen until the answer arrives. Unlike `ctrl+r`, this entry reload shows no
613	  spinner and no "Reading..." line, because `Init` cannot set `loading` to
614	  true. `ctrl+r` reads again under a new generation number, and a stale answer
615	  (older generation) is dropped. A failed refresh keeps the previous rows: they
616	  are dated, not wrong.
617	- **Rule 110.** `listSessionsCmd` resolves `ProjectsRoot()` and calls
618	  `ListSessions` inside the `Cmd` and returns a message; `Update` alone touches
619	  the model.
620	
621	### Second level: the session's agents (DEVDESK-42)
622	
623	`→`/`enter` on a session opens its agents; `←`/`esc` goes back to the list.
624	`agents.go` builds the table, `availability.go` decides what the keys allow.
625	
626	| Column | Content |
627	|---|---|
628	| Agent | `orchestrator`, then each sub-agent's type behind `├─ ` / `└─ ` in tree order, bare when sorted (`unknown` when the meta file gave none). `/` matches the role only. |

830	- `switchView` calls `Init()` on every entry; at the agents level `Init` adds
831	  `resumeCmd()`, which answers `agentsResumeMsg`. `handleResume` bumps
832	  `agentGen` again, clears `pollStopped` and starts a read from the cursor,
833	  silent: coming back reads what changed while away, and goes back to live if
834	  the session is still being written. With `fullPending`, the read is full and
835	  has its spinner.

838	stable key: `main` for the orchestrator, `sub:<ID>#n` for a sub-agent, `n`
839	counting the earlier agents with the same ID (two twins with one ID keep their
840	own keys). Keys are computed on the canonical order (`agentRows`), never on the
841	sorted or filtered one, otherwise twins would swap keys whenever they swap
842	ranks. `withUsage` records the key under the cursor before rebuilding the rows

and when a session ran at this level (see the privacy amendment above). `→` or
`enter` opens the selected session's agents (DEVDESK-42, below).

| Column | Content |
|---|---|
| Project | the `cwd`, **full path** with home folded to `~` (`theme.FoldHome`, done once per row in `Update`, never in a `Cell`). Cut from the left when too narrow, so the leaf stays visible. `-` (dim) when the transcript named none. |
| Last active | the transcript's `ModTime`, local time, `2006-01-02 15:04` |
| Session | the first 8 characters of the ID. `Optional`: the first column dropped on a narrow terminal. The filter (`/`) matches the full ID. |

- **Rule 139.** The body is always `m.table.View()`. Loading, an empty
  machine and a filter with no match all leave a table with its header.
- **Header** (`GetHeaderInfo`): `Sessions` (rows visible after the filter) and,
  only when non-zero, `Skipped` (`Listing.Omitted`).
- **Footer** (Rule 128), derived on every frame with no timer, in this order:
  a failed read (red, "Failed to list Claude Code sessions — check logs"; the
  error is logged, never shown, since it can name a path), then loading (spinner,
  "Reading Claude Code sessions..."), then "No Claude Code sessions found in
  <root>" when the listing is empty before any filter.

  state, none greyed (Rule 130): each always acts. `.` cycles the sort column
  and is listed in `?` only (Rule 138).

  router (`createView` stops if it already exists). The reload comes from
  `switchView` (`internal/app/command_line.go`), which calls `Init()` on every
  entry, and `Init` starts a read. The rows from the previous visit stay on

  spinner and no "Reading..." line, because `Init` cannot set `loading` to

#### Agent state and activity (DEVDESK-46)

`status.go` derives the State column. The package describes what the transcripts
say; what counts as "idle" is a display policy that depends on the view's clock,
so it lives here, not in `internal/agentusage`. `agentStates` is pure: the clock
is a parameter (`statusClock{now, alive}`).

- **`alive`** means the poll chain is live: `!Settled(at, quietPeriod)`. There is
  no other source (no process probe, no session registry): it also works for a
  transcript copied from elsewhere.
- **`quiet`** means `now - LastActivity > idleAfter` (5 min), **strictly**: at
  exactly 5 min an agent is still running. No timestamp, or a timestamp in the
  future (clock skew), is never quiet.
- **`now` is `usageDeltaMsg.at`**, the moment the read finished, not the wall
  clock at render time, so the same answer gives the same states on every frame.

| Agent | Condition | State |
|---|---|---|
| sub-agent | meta `finished: true` | `done` |
| sub-agent | meta `finished: false` | `running`, or `idle` when quiet, whether or not the session is alive |
| sub-agent | no `finished` key, session alive | `running` / `idle` as above |
| sub-agent | no `finished` key, session not alive | `unknown` |
| orchestrator | session alive | `running`, or `idle` when quiet **and no sub-agent is `running`** |
| orchestrator | session not alive | `unknown` |

The orchestrator is **never `done`**: Claude Code writes no end marker for it. A
foreground `Agent` call leaves it silent for as long as the sub-agent runs, so it
is not idle while one runs; if every running sub-agent is itself idle, it is idle
too. Once updates pause it reads `unknown`, so a session waiting at the prompt for
more than 5 min shows `unknown` and `Updates › paused`. Colours (Rule 122): `idle`
in the MEDIUM orange, `unknown` dim, `running` and `done` in the text colour.

**The rows are rebuilt on every successful read, even an empty one** (`applyRead`
in `update.go`). An agent turns idle precisely because nothing arrives, so an
empty delta must still move the clock. `settled` is computed once and used for
both the clock and the decision to stop polling; while a `ctrl+r` full read is
pending the session counts as alive, so the header does not flash `paused`.
`withUsage` is `withRows` plus clearing the loading and error flags; population
is unchanged on an empty delta, so there is no `Remeasure` and the selection
stays on its agent. On `os.ErrNotExist`, `failRead` marks the clock not alive and
calls `withRows` (not `withUsage`), so the red footer stays. Opening or leaving a
session resets the clock.

**Header.** `Idle › N` follows `Updates`, only when N > 0, counted over every row
(`agentTable.Items()`), not the filtered ones: an alert must not hide behind a
filter. No shortcut was added, so Rule 130's key set is unchanged.

**Known limits.**
1. *Idle is a hint.* A long tool call (a 10-minute test run) writes nothing and
   reads idle. The help says so.
2. *Duration is wall clock.* A resumed session spans days between its first and
   last line.
3. *Clock skew.* The idle test compares the transcript's clock with this
   machine's; a sandbox with a skewed clock shows wrong flags (a future timestamp
   is never idle, a past one is).
4. *A lone orchestrator pauses when it would turn idle.* The chain stops at the
   same 5 min, so it reads `unknown`, not `idle` (see "Known limits, deliberate").

#### Live updates (DEVDESK-45)

The agents level follows a session that is still being written. It uses the
incremental API of DEVDESK-44 (`Cursor`, `Delta`, `Aggregate`), not
`ParseSession`: the model holds one `*Aggregate` per open session, and each
read applies a `Delta` to it.

**The polling chain.** Opening a session starts a full read (cursor
`Rewound()`, spinner, "Reading session..."). Each answer schedules the next
step: wait `pollInterval` (2 s, `pollTickCmd`), then `startRead(false)` reads
from the cursor, silently (no spinner). At most one read and one tick exist per
`agentGen`: `reading` blocks a tick that arrives while a read is in flight, and
a tick or an answer of another generation is dropped. An empty delta changes
nothing on screen; a non-empty or full one rebuilds the rows (`withUsage`).
If `Aggregate.Apply` rejects a delta (not read from the current cursor), the
view logs it and reads again from the aggregate's own cursor.

**When the chain stops.** After a successful read, the chain ends if
`Activity().Settled(at, quietPeriod)` is true: `quietPeriod` is 5 min, and a
session with any sub-agent not finished is never settled (see "Activity and
`Settled`"). It also ends on `os.ErrNotExist` (the parent transcript was
deleted). Any other error retries after another 2 s from the same cursor and
keeps the rows already shown; the footer says "Failed to read this session —
check logs", and only the first failure of a streak is logged. A successful
read clears the error.

**`pollStopped`.** The model records the end of the chain as `pollStopped`
(true = stopped). The plan spoke of a `live` field; the code has the opposite
sense, so that the zero value of a fresh model is "polling". It makes a late
tick of the same generation start nothing, and every full read clears it.

**The `Updates` header.** `Updates › live` while an aggregate is open and
`pollStopped` is false, `paused` otherwise. It is derived on every frame
(`updatesState`), not stored. Pressing `ctrl+r` on a settled session clears
`pollStopped` for the duration of the full read, so the header can go
`paused → live → paused` in a few frames when the session is still quiet.

**`ctrl+r` is a full read.** It rewinds the cursor (`Cursor.Rewound()`), reads
everything again, and shows the spinner. If a read is already in flight, it is
never doubled (one per `Aggregate`): `fullPending` is set and the full read
starts when that read answers, whether it succeeded or failed.

**Leaving and coming back** (`LeavingView`, see `app-shell.md`).
- `Leave()` bumps `agentGen`, which drops any tick or read in flight, and
  clears `reading` and `agentsLoading`. The open session and its rows stay. If
  a full read was in flight (a `ctrl+r`, or the open's first read), `Leave` sets
  `fullPending`, so the resume repeats it. It always returns `true`.
- `switchView` calls `Init()` on every entry; at the agents level `Init` adds
  `resumeCmd()`, which answers `agentsResumeMsg`. `handleResume` bumps
  `agentGen` again, clears `pollStopped` and starts a read from the cursor,
  silent: coming back reads what changed while away, and goes back to live if
  the session is still being written. With `fullPending`, the read is full and
  has its spinner.

**The cursor stays on the same agent.** `selection.go` gives each agent a
stable key: `main` for the orchestrator, `sub:<ID>#n` for a sub-agent, `n`
counting the earlier agents with the same ID (two twins with one ID keep their
own keys). Keys are computed on the canonical order (`agentRows`), never on the
sorted or filtered one, otherwise twins would swap keys whenever they swap
ranks. `withUsage` records the key under the cursor before rebuilding the rows

162	### Per-model tokens (DEVDESK-47)
163	
164	`Agent.ByModel` splits `Agent.Tokens` by model, in first-appearance order, with
165	the bucket of `Model == ""` last. That bucket holds messages that name no model
166	and the models past the cap of 64 per agent (`maxModelsPerAgent`, the cap that
167	already applies to `Models`). The sum of `ByModel` is `Agent.Tokens`, also past
168	the cap and for the lines that spill (`modelTally`, in `limits.go`).
169	
170	Each usage line may carry `usage.cache_creation.ephemeral_1h_input_tokens`: the
171	part of `cache_creation_input_tokens` written with the 1 h cache, which is
172	priced differently from the 5 min one. It is decoded apart, so a value of
173	another shape costs the split and nothing else: an absent, negative,
174	fractional, text or null value is 0, the line stays a usage line, and the token
175	totals do not move. A value above the total is clamped to the total. As for the
176	other counters, the last line of a message wins. `ModelUsage.CacheWrite5m()` is
177	`Tokens.CacheWrite - CacheWrite1h`. Checked on 49 real parent transcripts: the
178	field is on every usage line, 5 min + 1 h equals the total write on all of
179	them, and 1 h writes are 47 % of the cache written. Pricing every write at one
180	rate would be wrong by a large factor, which is why the split exists.

182	### `cost-state` and `Billed` (DEVDESK-47)
183	
184	Claude Code appends a line of root `type` `cost-state` when a session closes. It
185	has no `message` and no `timestamp`; the package reads three keys of it, and no
186	others: `type`, `sessionId`, `totalCostUSD`. It is a `kindCostState` line
187	(`record.go`): it counts for nothing else (no tokens, no version, no activity).
188	
189	`Usage.Billed` is `Billed{USD, Known}`. `Known` is true only when all of these
190	hold:
191	
192	- the cost-state line with the greatest position **in the parent transcript** is
193	  also the parent's last complete line (`parentEnd`, the greatest position of
194	  any complete parent line, readable or not, oversized included);
195	- its `totalCostUSD` is a finite number >= 0;
196	- its `sessionId` equals the session's, or is absent or null (any other value
197	  matches no session).
198	
199	A cost-state line in a sub-agent file is ignored. Both positions are maxima, so
200	a merge is commutative and the incremental result still equals `ParseSession`
201	(see "Incremental reading"). `table.hasLines()` counts the cost-state, so the
202	delta that brings it is not `Empty()` and the view rebuilds; as a consequence a
203	cost-state counts as file activity for `Activity.LastChange`, and updates pause
204	up to 5 min later than before.
205	
206	What 46 of 49 real parents here show (one client version line, 2.1.28x to
207	2.1.30x): the line is always last in the file; a session resumed and closed again
208	appends a new **cumulative** cost-state (7.08 then 12.61 in one file), so the
209	last one is the bill. This is observed, not documented by Claude Code.

211	**Known limit, declared.** Billed goes stale after a line that carries no
212	timestamp and no usage (the delta has no activity to move the view), because the
213	view only rebuilds on a non-empty delta that changes something. It is corrected
214	by the next line with a timestamp, or by `ctrl+r`. The test file states it.

217	1 h split, a first cost-state (7.08), more usage, then a second cumulative one

796	nothing on screen; a non-empty or full one rebuilds the rows (`withUsage`).
797	If `Aggregate.Apply` rejects a delta (not read from the current cursor), the
798	view logs it and reads again from the aggregate's own cursor.
799	
800	**When the chain stops.** After a successful read, the chain ends if
801	`Activity().Settled(at, quietPeriod)` is true: `quietPeriod` is 5 min, and a
802	session with any sub-agent not finished is never settled (see "Activity and
803	`Settled`"). It also ends on `os.ErrNotExist` (the parent transcript was
804	deleted). Any other error retries after another 2 s from the same cursor and
805	keeps the rows already shown; the footer says "Failed to read this session —
806	check logs", and only the first failure of a streak is logged. A successful
807	read clears the error.
808	
809	**`pollStopped`.** The model records the end of the chain as `pollStopped`
810	(true = stopped). The plan spoke of a `live` field; the code has the opposite
811	sense, so that the zero value of a fresh model is "polling". It makes a late
812	tick of the same generation start nothing, and every full read clears it.
813	
814	**The `Updates` header.** `Updates › live` while an aggregate is open and
815	`pollStopped` is false, `paused` otherwise. It is derived on every frame
816	(`updatesState`), not stored. Pressing `ctrl+r` on a settled session clears
817	`pollStopped` for the duration of the full read, so the header can go
818	`paused → live → paused` in a few frames when the session is still quiet.
819	
820	**`ctrl+r` is a full read.** It rewinds the cursor (`Cursor.Rewound()`), reads
821	everything again, and shows the spinner. If a read is already in flight, it is
822	never doubled (one per `Aggregate`): `fullPending` is set and the full read
823	starts when that read answers, whether it succeeded or failed.
824	
825	**Leaving and coming back** (`LeavingView`, see `app-shell.md`).
826	- `Leave()` bumps `agentGen`, which drops any tick or read in flight, and
827	  clears `reading` and `agentsLoading`. The open session and its rows stay. If
828	  a full read was in flight (a `ctrl+r`, or the open's first read), `Leave` sets
829	  `fullPending`, so the resume repeats it. It always returns `true`.
830	- `switchView` calls `Init()` on every entry; at the agents level `Init` adds
831	  `resumeCmd()`, which answers `agentsResumeMsg`. `handleResume` bumps
832	  `agentGen` again, clears `pollStopped` and starts a read from the cursor,
833	  silent: coming back reads what changed while away, and goes back to live if
834	  the session is still being written. With `fullPending`, the read is full and
835	  has its spinner.
836	
837	**The cursor stays on the same agent.** `selection.go` gives each agent a
838	stable key: `main` for the orchestrator, `sub:<ID>#n` for a sub-agent, `n`
839	counting the earlier agents with the same ID (two twins with one ID keep their
840	own keys). Keys are computed on the canonical order (`agentRows`), never on the
841	sorted or filtered one, otherwise twins would swap keys whenever they swap
842	ranks. `withUsage` records the key under the cursor before rebuilding the rows

1	// Package keymap declares the application's keyboard vocabulary.
2	//
3	// It does not read any key and does not depend on bubbletea: it is a list of
4	// strings, and its only role is to be the reference the tests check the code
5	// against (keymap_test.go). Without this reference, key consistency is a
6	// convention that nothing verifies — which is exactly the state §3.26 found:
7	// 184 bindings, 16 collisions.
8	//
9	// # Three disjoint namespaces
10	//
11	//   - An UPPERCASE letter is an action, and its meaning is global to the
12	//     application. `D` deletes, in every view, whatever "delete" means
13	//     wherever you are.
14	//   - A lowercase letter is a filter or a display toggle. It changes
15	//     nothing, so its meaning can be local and two views can use the same
16	//     letter without contradicting each other.
17	//   - Everything else (arrows, esc, enter, tab, space, `/`, `.`, `?`, `:`) is
18	//     structural and never changes.
19	//
20	// # Why Shift carries the actions
21	//
22	// This isn't a matter of taste, it's the real budget of a terminal:
23	//
24	//	Ctrl+letter  : only encodes ASCII 0x40-0x5F, and the tty confiscates
25	//	               four of them (ctrl+i = TAB, ctrl+m = Enter, ctrl+j = LF,
26	//	               ctrl+h = Backspace). ctrl+a and ctrl+b are screen's and
27	//	               tmux's prefixes, ctrl+c/ctrl+d are SIGINT and EOF,
28	//	               ctrl+s/ctrl+q are flow control.           → ~14 left
29	//	Alt+key      : Option is not Meta on macOS unless the user enables it;
30	//	               the application receives nothing.                → 0
31	//	Ctrl+Shift   : the control code erases case — ctrl+a and ctrl+shift+a
32	//	               both emit 0x01. Telling them apart requires the Kitty
33	//	               keyboard protocol or modifyOtherKeys, which bubbletea
34	//	               v1.3.10 does not enable (that's WithKeyboardEnhancements()
35	//	               in v2). And even then the emulator claims them first:
36	//	               ctrl+shift+c/v/t/w/n are copy, paste, tab, close, window.
37	//	                                                                  → 0
38	//	Shift+letter : no constraint. Works on every emulator, every platform,
39	//	               through SSH and tmux.                             → 26
40	//
41	// Shift+letter IS a two-key combination: two fingers, no accidental firing.
42	// It carries the vocabulary not by default, but because the two other
43	// families are crippled or unusable.
44	package keymap
45	
46	import (
47		"maps"
48		"sort"
49		"strings"
50	)
51	
52	// The 24 actions. About forty actions used to exist for 26 letters: the
53	// rule only holds after merging synonyms (Kill = stop and kill,
54	// Delete = delete and remove, Terminal = terminal and shell) and because
55	// display toggles are excluded from the count.
56	const (
57		New      = "N" // Create a resource from this context
58		Edit     = "E" // Edit the selected resource
59		Delete   = "D" // Delete the selected resource
60		Rename   = "M" // Rename (mv)
61		Scan     = "S" // Scan the selected target
62		ScanAll  = "A" // Scan everything (modal: "purge the cache first" checkbox)
63		Fetch    = "F" // Catch up with the source: fetch + fast-forward, or follow a stream
64		Clone    = "C" // Enter clone selection
65		Terminal = "T" // Open a terminal or shell
66		IDE      = "O" // Open in the configured IDE
67		Web      = "W" // Open a URL in the browser
68		Logs     = "L" // Open the logs
69		Pager    = "V" // Open in the system pager
70		Kill     = "K" // Stop, kill (modal: Stop / Restart, or SIGKILL)
71		Prune    = "P" // Remove unused resources
72		Browser  = "B" // Open the multi-registry browser
73		Get      = "G" // Pull (get) the image or tag
74		Auth     = "U" // Login / logout of the registry — toggles based on the row's state
75		Exclude  = "X" // Exclude — add to .gitleaksignore
76		Requests = "R" // Open merge requests · PRs
77		Issues   = "I" // Open issues
78		Diagnose = "H" // Open network diagnostics on this target
79		// Jump took J from the free letters: it opens the selected row's related
80		// resource in the view that owns it — the image a container runs, today.
81		Jump = "J" // Jump to the related resource in its own view
82		// Copy is `Y` — yank. The letter was free even though a modal uses it
83		// for "Yes": a modal claims every key before the view sees it, so the
84		// two are never reachable at the same time.
85		Copy = "Y" // Copy the obvious thing to the clipboard — a path, a document's content, the MCP connect command
86	)
87	
88	// CommandMode opens the command palette, from anywhere — including from a
89	// focused text field.
90	//
91	// ctrl+p, and not ctrl+: : ":" is 0x3A, outside the 0x40-0x5F range Ctrl
92	// encodes, so "ctrl+:" never reaches the application. The fallback was
93	// alt+:, which has the opposite flaw: on Terminal.app and iTerm2,
94	// Option+Shift+; emits a literal character and the key doesn't arrive
95	// either. ctrl+p is free throughout the application, is not a tty control
96	// character, is not the prefix of any multiplexer, and its meaning is
97	// already learned — command palette.
98	const CommandMode = "ctrl+p"
99	
100	// actions maps each action key to its meaning. This is the table the tests
101	// check the code against; the table in §3.26 is its readable form.
102	var actions = map[string]string{
103		New:      "Create a resource from this context",
104		Edit:     "Edit the selected resource",
105		Delete:   "Delete the selected resource",
106		Rename:   "Rename",
107		Scan:     "Scan the selected target",
108		ScanAll:  "Scan everything",
109		Fetch:    "Catch up with the source",
110		Clone:    "Enter clone selection",
111		Terminal: "Open a terminal or shell",
112		IDE:      "Open in the configured IDE",
113		Web:      "Open a URL in the browser",
114		Logs:     "Open the logs",
115		Pager:    "Open in the system pager",
116		Kill:     "Stop or kill",
117		Prune:    "Remove unused resources",
118		Browser:  "Open the multi-registry browser",
119		Get:      "Pull the image or tag",
120		Auth:     "Log in or out of the registry",
121		Exclude:  "Exclude — add to .gitleaksignore",
122		Requests: "Open merge requests · PRs",
123		Issues:   "Open issues",
124		Diagnose: "Open network diagnostics on this target",
125		Jump:     "Jump to the related resource in its own view",
126		Copy:     "Copy the obvious thing to the clipboard",
127	}
128	
129	// Actions returns a copy of the key → meaning table.
130	func Actions() map[string]string {
131		out := make(map[string]string, len(actions))
132		maps.Copy(out, actions)
133		return out
134	}
135	
136	// IsAction reports whether a key belongs to the action vocabulary.
137	func IsAction(key string) bool {
138		_, ok := actions[key]
139		return ok
140	}
141	
142	// modalKeys are the shortcuts of a confirmation modal.
143	//
144	// This is a fourth namespace, and it is disjoint from the other three by
145	// mode rather than by case: a modal claims every key before the view sees
146	// it (priority 1 in every handleKeyMsg), so `N` cannot mean "create" there
147	// — the view underneath receives nothing. Same argument as for InEditMode.
148	//
149	// They are declared here because the §3.26 survey had not seen them, and
150	// an uppercase letter bound without a declaration is indistinguishable
151	// from drift.
152	var modalKeys = map[string]string{
153		"y": "Yes", "Y": "Yes",
154		"n": "No", "N": "No",
155	}
156	
157	// ModalKeys returns the modal shortcuts.
158	func ModalKeys() map[string]string {
159		out := make(map[string]string, len(modalKeys))
160		maps.Copy(out, modalKeys)
161		return out
162	}
163	
164	// IsModalKey reports whether a key is a modal shortcut.
165	func IsModalKey(key string) bool {
166		_, ok := modalKeys[key]
167		return ok
168	}
169	
170	// free lists the uppercase letters no action occupies. They are declared
171	// rather than left to be inferred: the next addition must know where to
172	// pick from without redoing the survey, and an action that settles
173	// somewhere other than here is a duplicate that goes unnoticed.
174	// H came back here with §3.47 (it used to trace the route, removed because
175	// it answered for the Docker VM rather than for the machine, D57) and left
176	// again with Diagnose (§3.66): a good semantic fit for "look closer at this
177	// target's network path." A letter an action has just freed up is
178	// re-declared free, otherwise it stays reserved for a use that no longer
179	// exists. J left with Jump (a container's image, opened in the OCI view).
180	var free = []string{"Q", "Z"}
181	
182	// Free returns the still-available uppercase letters, sorted.
183	func Free() []string {
184		out := append([]string(nil), free...)
185		sort.Strings(out)
186		return out
187	}
188	
189	// Surface is a screen, its files, and the lowercase letters it uses.
190	//
191	// Path is what ties a file to its surface, and it is there so the
192	// declaration is checkable: without it, "these letters are local to this
193	// view" is verified by merging every list, and `l` declared for netdiag
194	// would excuse `l` in the registries. Matching is done on the longest
195	// prefix, so netdiag/ports can narrow down netdiag.
196	type Surface struct {
197		Name string
198		Path string
199		Keys []string
200	}
201	
202	// localToggles inventories the lowercase letters used as display or filter
203	// toggles. They change nothing, so their meaning is local and the same
204	// letter can serve twice without contradiction — `l` is the protocol in
205	// netdiag and the LOW severity in security.
206	//
207	// A file that matches no surface is entitled to no lowercase letter at
208	// all: that is the default, and it is what makes the list worth keeping
209	// up to date.
210	var localToggles = []Surface{
211		{"containers", "ui/containers/", []string{"r", "p", "s", "t", "z"}},
212		{"viewer", "ui/viewer/", []string{"f", "c", "w", "v", "t", "n", "g", "s"}},
213		{"netdiag/ports", "ui/netdiag/ports_model.go", []string{"t", "u", "l", "e", "n", "z"}},
214		{"netdiag/checks", "ui/netdiag/", []string{"p"}},
215		{"oci/browser", "ui/oci_resources/browser_", []string{"r"}},
216		{"security/findings", "ui/security/", []string{"c", "h", "m", "l"}},
217		// g opens the fuzzy-find prompt across the whole workspaces tree. Same
218		// justification as the viewer's g: the jump takes an argument (the typed
219		// query), which is not a role home/end/G could ever cover.
220		{"workspaces", "ui/workspaces/", []string{"g"}},
221		// The same prompt over the forge index: every namespace and repository
222		// the session can see, at any depth.
223		{"forge/explorer", "ui/forge/explorer/", []string{"g"}},
224	}
225	
226	// LocalToggles returns the declared surfaces.
227	func LocalToggles() []Surface {
228		return append([]Surface(nil), localToggles...)
229	}
230	
231	// SurfaceFor ties a file path to its surface, by longest prefix. The
232	// second return says whether a surface was found.
233	func SurfaceFor(path string) (Surface, bool) {
234		var best Surface
235		found := false
236		for _, s := range localToggles {
237			if !strings.Contains(path, s.Path) {
238				continue
239			}
240			if !found || len(s.Path) > len(best.Path) {
241				best, found = s, true
242			}
243		}
244		return best, found
245	}
246	
247	// Exception is a key that deviates from the vocabulary, with its reason.
248	type Exception struct {
249		Key     string
250		Surface string
251		Why     string
252	}
253	
254	// exceptions are the accepted deviations. They are written here
255	// because §3.26 requires it: an undeclared exception is indistinguishable
256	// from drift, and the next survey would "fix" it.
257	var exceptions = []Exception{
258		{
259			Key:     "o",
260			Surface: "security/results/ci-tab",
261			Why: "Ouvrir le pipeline résolu par le forge. Même raison que `c` : " +
262				"l'action n'existe que sur un onglet, et brûler une des trois " +
263				"dernières majuscules libres pour ça coûterait plus que ça ne " +
264				"rapporte. `o` plutôt qu'une autre lettre parce qu'il veut déjà " +
265				"dire « ouvrir ce que cet écran désigne » dans l'état détail de " +
266				"la même vue, où il ouvre la référence d'un finding.",
267		},
268		{
269			Key:     "ctrl+y",
270			Surface: "oci/launch-form",
271			Why: "Copier la commande docker run. Même raison, et ctrl+y ne heurte " +
272				"aucun caractère de contrôle utilisé ailleurs.",
273		},
274		{
275			Key:     "ctrl+o",
276			Surface: "security/results/remediation-tab",
277			Why: "Write the chosen base images into the Dockerfiles. The action " +
278				"exists on one tab, so a global capital would cost more than it " +
279				"returns. ^O is Write Out in nano; bubbletea puts the terminal in " +
280				"raw mode, which switches off the only other job ^O has in a tty " +
281				"(discard output). The obvious alternatives are taken: ctrl+w closes " +
282				"a browser or web-terminal tab, ctrl+s is flow control, and ctrl+d is " +
283				"end-of-file.",
284		},
285		{
286			Key:     "tab",
287			Surface: "app/command-line",
288			Why: "Complete the highlighted suggestion. The command palette has no tabs " +
289				"and no fields, so tab's usual jobs (Rule 135: switch tabs, never " +
290				"move between fields) do not exist there, and completing is what " +
291				"tab means in every shell. Nothing is run: enter does that.",
292		},
293	}
294	
295	// DeclaredExceptions returns the declared exceptions.
296	func DeclaredExceptions() []Exception {
297		return append([]Exception(nil), exceptions...)
298	}
299	
300	// IsException reports whether a key is a declared exception on a surface.
301	func IsException(key string) bool {
302		for _, e := range exceptions {
303			if e.Key == key {
304				return true
305			}
306		}
307		return false
308	}

1	package theme
2	
3	import (
4		"math"
5		"strings"
6	
7		"github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss"
8	
9		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/config"
10	)
11	
12	// A load gauge: a bar that answers "is something hot" without reading a
13	// number (§3.71).
14	//
15	// By default every cell is the same glyph — `░` — used or not. What used to
16	// tell a filled cell from an empty one by shape then does it by colour alone:
17	// LoadTextStyle on the fill, GaugeTrackStyle on the track, split by
18	// datatable.Column.Cut after the text is already measured (Rule 122). A value
19	// survives the row disappearing under the cursor only through the number
20	// beside the gauge — Style is not consulted on the selected row, and with one
21	// glyph the bar itself has nothing left to say once its colour is gone.
22	//
23	// `app.gauge_glyph: block` opts into a solid `█` fill over the `░` track,
24	// which keeps that shape under the cursor. It is an opt-in because `█` is
25	// East Asian ambiguous width (see gaugeGlyph): the user, not the locale,
26	// knows how their terminal draws it.
27	
28	// gaugeGlyph is the glyph of the track, and of the fill by default. `░` is a
29	// Block Elements glyph, and the *only* one of the family that measures 1 cell
30	// in both the default and the East Asian `runewidth` condition — every other
31	// glyph in the range (`█`, `▓`, `▇`, the partial blocks `▏▎▍▌`) is *ambiguous*
32	// and renders double-width on some terminals, which would overflow the
33	// column and break Rule 116. Measured, not assumed.
34	const gaugeGlyph = "░"
35	
36	// gaugeBlockGlyph is the fill the "block" gauge style swaps in. Ambiguous
37	// width, hence never the default: a terminal that draws it double-width
38	// overflows every gauge column, and only the user can know that.
39	const gaugeBlockGlyph = "█"
40	
41	// gaugeFillGlyph is the glyph the filled cells render, set once from
42	// app.gauge_glyph by SetGaugeGlyph. Process-wide state like the palette
43	// ApplyTheme writes: it is only touched from Update() and read while
44	// rendering, both on the Bubble Tea loop.
45	var gaugeFillGlyph = gaugeGlyph
46	
47	// SetGaugeGlyph selects the fill glyph from an app.gauge_glyph value. Anything
48	// but "block" — including a typo in the file — is the safe `░`.
49	func SetGaugeGlyph(style string) {
50		if style == config.GaugeGlyphBlock {
51			gaugeFillGlyph = gaugeBlockGlyph
52			return
53		}
54		gaugeFillGlyph = gaugeGlyph
55	}
56	
57	// GaugeWidth is the width of a gauge column, in cells.
58	//
59	// Ten: with a single glyph carrying no shape of its own, resolution is one
60	// cell per `GaugeWidth`th of the scale — 10% here — and a wider bar reads
61	// better than a narrower one at the same resolution the old half-braille
62	// design gave for six. The number beside it still carries the exact value.
63	const GaugeWidth = 10
64	
65	// Load thresholds, in percent: green, then orange, then red — the colour a
66	// *filled* cell takes; GaugeTrackStyle below is what an *empty* one always
67	// takes, whatever the level.
68	const (
69		// LoadWarnPercent is where a gauge stops being ordinary: filling up, and
70		// worth noticing.
71		LoadWarnPercent = 75
72		// LoadCriticalPercent is where it is nearly full — the memory gauge's
73		// reading of a container about to meet its limit.
74		LoadCriticalPercent = 90
75	)
76	
77	// Gauge renders a bar of width cells at pct, as plain text: GaugeFillWidth
78	// fill glyphs, then track glyphs. In the default style the two are the same
79	// character and the value lives entirely in how many cells a caller colours
80	// with LoadTextStyle rather than GaugeTrackStyle (datatable.Column.Cut, after
81	// measurement — never inside this string); with "block" the text carries the
82	// split too.
83	func Gauge(pct float64, width int) string {
84		return GaugeFill(GaugeFillWidth(pct, width)) + GaugeTrack(width-GaugeFillWidth(pct, width))
85	}
86	
87	// GaugeFill renders n filled cells, for a caller that styles the two runs
88	// itself (a waterfall bar).
89	func GaugeFill(n int) string {
90		if n <= 0 {
91			return ""
92		}
93		return strings.Repeat(gaugeFillGlyph, n)
94	}
95	
96	// GaugeTrack renders n empty cells. Always `░`, whatever the fill is.
97	func GaugeTrack(n int) string {
98		if n <= 0 {
99			return ""
100		}
101		return strings.Repeat(gaugeGlyph, n)
102	}
103	
104	// GaugeFillWidth reports how many of Gauge's width cells count as filled —
105	// the boundary datatable.Column.Cut needs to hand LoadTextStyle the first
106	// cells and GaugeTrackStyle the rest.
107	//
108	// pct is clamped: anything at or above 100 fills the bar. Saturation is
109	// therefore indistinguishable from exactly full, which is deliberate and is
110	// the reason a gauge never replaces the number beside it — `docker stats`
111	// counts CPU against one core, so two busy cores read 200% and only the
112	// number tells the two apart (§3.71).
113	//
114	// Rounding is honest at the low end too: a container at 0.1% fills zero
115	// cells rather than one. A tenth of the bar *is* 10%, so lighting one for a
116	// value near zero would overstate it on every idle row — and idle is what
117	// most rows are.
118	func GaugeFillWidth(pct float64, width int) int {
119		if width <= 0 {
120			return 0
121		}
122		switch {
123		case math.IsNaN(pct), pct < 0:
124			pct = 0
125		case pct > 100:
126			pct = 100
127		}
128		return int(math.Round(pct / 100 * float64(width)))
129	}
130	
131	// LoadTextStyle is the colour a gauge's *filled* cells take at pct: green,
132	// then orange, then red. It follows SeverityTextStyle's shape — the view
133	// names a value, the theme answers with a colour — and it aliases the
134	// severity palette for the same reason the footer levels do (Rule 128): one
135	// alphabet across the application, so a full gauge reads like a CRITICAL
136	// finding.
137	//
138	// It is a function rather than a package-level style because the thresholds
139	// are the whole of it; a var per level would leave the switch in the view,
140	// which is where Rule 125 says a colour must not be decided.
141	func LoadTextStyle(pct float64) lipgloss.Style {
142		base := lipgloss.NewStyle().Background(ColorBackground)
143		switch {
144		case pct >= LoadCriticalPercent:
145			return base.Foreground(ColorSeverityCritical).Bold(true)
146		case pct >= LoadWarnPercent:
147			return base.Foreground(ColorSeverityMedium)
148		default:
149			return base.Foreground(ColorOK)
150		}
151	}
152	
153	// TimingBarWidth is the width of a waterfall bar (§3.66), in cells — wider
154	// than GaugeWidth: a waterfall has several phases to tell apart on one line,
155	// where a gauge answers a single percentage, and the extra resolution is what
156	// keeps a phase as small as a handful of percent visible at all.
157	const TimingBarWidth = 24
158	
159	// TimingFillStyle is the colour a waterfall bar's filled cells take (§3.66) —
160	// reusing Gauge/GaugeFillWidth for the glyph and the rounding, but not
161	// LoadTextStyle for the colour: a phase taking most of a request's time is
162	// not a problem to spot, just a fact to read, so it gets one neutral colour
163	// rather than a severity gradient. ColorSecondary is what headers and active
164	// tabs already use for structural information, which is the same role here.
165	func TimingFillStyle() lipgloss.Style {
166		return lipgloss.NewStyle().Background(ColorBackground).Foreground(ColorSecondary)
167	}
168	
169	// GaugeTrackStyle is the colour a gauge's *empty* cells take — fixed,
170	// whatever the level, including a gauge that is entirely empty: the cell is
171	// still `░`, still coloured, never blank. It aliases ColorSeverityLow rather
172	// than DimStyle directly: DimStyle is this application's word for *absent*
173	// (a `-`, a zero, a placeholder), and an empty gauge cell is not absent — it
174	// is measured and low. ColorSeverityLow's own default now happens to be the
175	// same tone as ColorDim (a LOW finding reads as unremarkable as a "0" count,
176	// see colors.go) — the two coincide in colour without coinciding in name, so
177	// a theme separating "low severity" from "nothing found" moves the track
178	// with the former rather than the latter.
179	func GaugeTrackStyle() lipgloss.Style {
180		return lipgloss.NewStyle().Background(ColorBackground).Foreground(ColorSeverityLow)
181	}

1	// Package keymap declares the application's keyboard vocabulary.
2	//
3	// It does not read any key and does not depend on bubbletea: it is a list of
4	// strings, and its only role is to be the reference the tests check the code
5	// against (keymap_test.go). Without this reference, key consistency is a
6	// convention that nothing verifies — which is exactly the state §3.26 found:
7	// 184 bindings, 16 collisions.
8	//
9	// # Three disjoint namespaces
10	//
11	//   - An UPPERCASE letter is an action, and its meaning is global to the
12	//     application. `D` deletes, in every view, whatever "delete" means
13	//     wherever you are.
14	//   - A lowercase letter is a filter or a display toggle. It changes
15	//     nothing, so its meaning can be local and two views can use the same
16	//     letter without contradicting each other.
17	//   - Everything else (arrows, esc, enter, tab, space, `/`, `.`, `?`, `:`) is
18	//     structural and never changes.
19	//
20	// # Why Shift carries the actions
21	//
22	// This isn't a matter of taste, it's the real budget of a terminal:
23	//
24	//	Ctrl+letter  : only encodes ASCII 0x40-0x5F, and the tty confiscates
25	//	               four of them (ctrl+i = TAB, ctrl+m = Enter, ctrl+j = LF,
26	//	               ctrl+h = Backspace). ctrl+a and ctrl+b are screen's and
27	//	               tmux's prefixes, ctrl+c/ctrl+d are SIGINT and EOF,
28	//	               ctrl+s/ctrl+q are flow control.           → ~14 left
29	//	Alt+key      : Option is not Meta on macOS unless the user enables it;
30	//	               the application receives nothing.                → 0
31	//	Ctrl+Shift   : the control code erases case — ctrl+a and ctrl+shift+a
32	//	               both emit 0x01. Telling them apart requires the Kitty
33	//	               keyboard protocol or modifyOtherKeys, which bubbletea
34	//	               v1.3.10 does not enable (that's WithKeyboardEnhancements()
35	//	               in v2). And even then the emulator claims them first:
36	//	               ctrl+shift+c/v/t/w/n are copy, paste, tab, close, window.
37	//	                                                                  → 0
38	//	Shift+letter : no constraint. Works on every emulator, every platform,
39	//	               through SSH and tmux.                             → 26
40	//
41	// Shift+letter IS a two-key combination: two fingers, no accidental firing.
42	// It carries the vocabulary not by default, but because the two other
43	// families are crippled or unusable.
44	package keymap
45	
46	import (
47		"maps"
48		"sort"
49		"strings"
50	)

52	// The 24 actions. About forty actions used to exist for 26 letters: the
53	// rule only holds after merging synonyms (Kill = stop and kill,
54	// Delete = delete and remove, Terminal = terminal and shell) and because
55	// display toggles are excluded from the count.
56	const (
57		New      = "N" // Create a resource from this context
58		Edit     = "E" // Edit the selected resource
59		Delete   = "D" // Delete the selected resource
60		Rename   = "M" // Rename (mv)
61		Scan     = "S" // Scan the selected target
62		ScanAll  = "A" // Scan everything (modal: "purge the cache first" checkbox)
63		Fetch    = "F" // Catch up with the source: fetch + fast-forward, or follow a stream
64		Clone    = "C" // Enter clone selection
65		Terminal = "T" // Open a terminal or shell
66		IDE      = "O" // Open in the configured IDE
67		Web      = "W" // Open a URL in the browser
68		Logs     = "L" // Open the logs
69		Pager    = "V" // Open in the system pager
70		Kill     = "K" // Stop, kill (modal: Stop / Restart, or SIGKILL)
71		Prune    = "P" // Remove unused resources
72		Browser  = "B" // Open the multi-registry browser
73		Get      = "G" // Pull (get) the image or tag

75		Exclude  = "X" // Exclude — add to .gitleaksignore

170	// free lists the uppercase letters no action occupies. They are declared
171	// rather than left to be inferred: the next addition must know where to
172	// pick from without redoing the survey, and an action that settles
173	// somewhere other than here is a duplicate that goes unnoticed.
174	// H came back here with §3.47 (it used to trace the route, removed because
175	// it answered for the Docker VM rather than for the machine, D57) and left

178	// re-declared free, otherwise it stays reserved for a use that no longer
179	// exists. J left with Jump (a container's image, opened in the OCI view).
180	var free = []string{"Q", "Z"}

189	// Surface is a screen, its files, and the lowercase letters it uses.

192	// declaration is checkable: without it, "these letters are local to this
193	// view" is verified by merging every list, and `l` declared for netdiag
194	// would excuse `l` in the registries. Matching is done on the longest
195	// prefix, so netdiag/ports can narrow down netdiag.

203	// toggles. They change nothing, so their meaning is local and the same
204	// letter can serve twice without contradiction — `l` is the protocol in
205	// netdiag and the LOW severity in security.

208	// all: that is the default, and it is what makes the list worth keeping
209	// up to date.
210	var localToggles = []Surface{
211		{"containers", "ui/containers/", []string{"r", "p", "s", "t", "z"}},
212		{"viewer", "ui/viewer/", []string{"f", "c", "w", "v", "t", "n", "g", "s"}},
213		{"netdiag/ports", "ui/netdiag/ports_model.go", []string{"t", "u", "l", "e", "n", "z"}},
214		{"netdiag/checks", "ui/netdiag/", []string{"p"}},
215		{"oci/browser", "ui/oci_resources/browser_", []string{"r"}},
216		{"security/findings", "ui/security/", []string{"c", "h", "m", "l"}},
217		// g opens the fuzzy-find prompt across the whole workspaces tree. Same
218		// justification as the viewer's g: the jump takes an argument (the typed
219		// query), which is not a role home/end/G could ever cover.
220		{"workspaces", "ui/workspaces/", []string{"g"}},
221		// The same prompt over the forge index: every namespace and repository
222		// the session can see, at any depth.
223		{"forge/explorer", "ui/forge/explorer/", []string{"g"}},
224	}
225	
226	// LocalToggles returns the declared surfaces.
227	func LocalToggles() []Surface {
228		return append([]Surface(nil), localToggles...)
229	}

231	// SurfaceFor ties a file path to its surface, by longest prefix. The
232	// second return says whether a surface was found.
233	func SurfaceFor(path string) (Surface, bool) {
234		var best Surface
235		found := false
236		for _, s := range localToggles {
237			if !strings.Contains(path, s.Path) {
238				continue
239			}
240			if !found || len(s.Path) > len(best.Path) {
241				best, found = s, true
242			}
243		}
244		return best, found
245	}

283				"end-of-file.",
284		},
285		{

288			Why: "Complete the highlighted suggestion. The command palette has no tabs " +
289				"and no fields, so tab's usual jobs (Rule 135: switch tabs, never " +

291				"tab means in every shell. Nothing is run: enter does that.",
292		},

294	
295	// DeclaredExceptions returns the declared exceptions.

301	func IsException(key string) bool {
302		for _, e := range exceptions {

1	package theme
2	
3	import (
4		"math"
5		"strings"
6	
7		"github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss"
8	
9		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/config"
10	)
11	
12	// A load gauge: a bar that answers "is something hot" without reading a
13	// number (§3.71).
14	//
15	// By default every cell is the same glyph — `░` — used or not. What used to
16	// tell a filled cell from an empty one by shape then does it by colour alone:
17	// LoadTextStyle on the fill, GaugeTrackStyle on the track, split by
18	// datatable.Column.Cut after the text is already measured (Rule 122). A value
19	// survives the row disappearing under the cursor only through the number
20	// beside the gauge — Style is not consulted on the selected row, and with one
21	// glyph the bar itself has nothing left to say once its colour is gone.
22	//
23	// `app.gauge_glyph: block` opts into a solid `█` fill over the `░` track,
24	// which keeps that shape under the cursor. It is an opt-in because `█` is
25	// East Asian ambiguous width (see gaugeGlyph): the user, not the locale,
26	// knows how their terminal draws it.
27	
28	// gaugeGlyph is the glyph of the track, and of the fill by default. `░` is a
29	// Block Elements glyph, and the *only* one of the family that measures 1 cell
30	// in both the default and the East Asian `runewidth` condition — every other
31	// glyph in the range (`█`, `▓`, `▇`, the partial blocks `▏▎▍▌`) is *ambiguous*
32	// and renders double-width on some terminals, which would overflow the
33	// column and break Rule 116. Measured, not assumed.
34	const gaugeGlyph = "░"
35	
36	// gaugeBlockGlyph is the fill the "block" gauge style swaps in. Ambiguous
37	// width, hence never the default: a terminal that draws it double-width
38	// overflows every gauge column, and only the user can know that.
39	const gaugeBlockGlyph = "█"
40	
41	// gaugeFillGlyph is the glyph the filled cells render, set once from
42	// app.gauge_glyph by SetGaugeGlyph. Process-wide state like the palette
43	// ApplyTheme writes: it is only touched from Update() and read while
44	// rendering, both on the Bubble Tea loop.
45	var gaugeFillGlyph = gaugeGlyph
46	
47	// SetGaugeGlyph selects the fill glyph from an app.gauge_glyph value. Anything
48	// but "block" — including a typo in the file — is the safe `░`.
49	func SetGaugeGlyph(style string) {
50		if style == config.GaugeGlyphBlock {
51			gaugeFillGlyph = gaugeBlockGlyph
52			return
53		}
54		gaugeFillGlyph = gaugeGlyph
55	}
56	
57	// GaugeWidth is the width of a gauge column, in cells.
58	//
59	// Ten: with a single glyph carrying no shape of its own, resolution is one
60	// cell per `GaugeWidth`th of the scale — 10% here — and a wider bar reads
61	// better than a narrower one at the same resolution the old half-braille
62	// design gave for six. The number beside it still carries the exact value.
63	const GaugeWidth = 10
64	
65	// Load thresholds, in percent: green, then orange, then red — the colour a
66	// *filled* cell takes; GaugeTrackStyle below is what an *empty* one always
67	// takes, whatever the level.
68	const (
69		// LoadWarnPercent is where a gauge stops being ordinary: filling up, and
70		// worth noticing.
71		LoadWarnPercent = 75
72		// LoadCriticalPercent is where it is nearly full — the memory gauge's
73		// reading of a container about to meet its limit.
74		LoadCriticalPercent = 90
75	)
76	
77	// Gauge renders a bar of width cells at pct, as plain text: GaugeFillWidth
78	// fill glyphs, then track glyphs. In the default style the two are the same
79	// character and the value lives entirely in how many cells a caller colours
80	// with LoadTextStyle rather than GaugeTrackStyle (datatable.Column.Cut, after
81	// measurement — never inside this string); with "block" the text carries the
82	// split too.
83	func Gauge(pct float64, width int) string {
84		return GaugeFill(GaugeFillWidth(pct, width)) + GaugeTrack(width-GaugeFillWidth(pct, width))
85	}
86	
87	// GaugeFill renders n filled cells, for a caller that styles the two runs
88	// itself (a waterfall bar).
89	func GaugeFill(n int) string {
90		if n <= 0 {
91			return ""
92		}
93		return strings.Repeat(gaugeFillGlyph, n)
94	}
95	
96	// GaugeTrack renders n empty cells. Always `░`, whatever the fill is.
97	func GaugeTrack(n int) string {
98		if n <= 0 {
99			return ""
100		}
101		return strings.Repeat(gaugeGlyph, n)
102	}
103	
104	// GaugeFillWidth reports how many of Gauge's width cells count as filled —
105	// the boundary datatable.Column.Cut needs to hand LoadTextStyle the first
106	// cells and GaugeTrackStyle the rest.
107	//
108	// pct is clamped: anything at or above 100 fills the bar. Saturation is
109	// therefore indistinguishable from exactly full, which is deliberate and is
110	// the reason a gauge never replaces the number beside it — `docker stats`
111	// counts CPU against one core, so two busy cores read 200% and only the
112	// number tells the two apart (§3.71).
113	//
114	// Rounding is honest at the low end too: a container at 0.1% fills zero
115	// cells rather than one. A tenth of the bar *is* 10%, so lighting one for a
116	// value near zero would overstate it on every idle row — and idle is what
117	// most rows are.
118	func GaugeFillWidth(pct float64, width int) int {
119		if width <= 0 {
120			return 0
121		}
122		switch {
123		case math.IsNaN(pct), pct < 0:
124			pct = 0
125		case pct > 100:
126			pct = 100
127		}
128		return int(math.Round(pct / 100 * float64(width)))
129	}
130	
131	// LoadTextStyle is the colour a gauge's *filled* cells take at pct: green,
132	// then orange, then red. It follows SeverityTextStyle's shape — the view
133	// names a value, the theme answers with a colour — and it aliases the
134	// severity palette for the same reason the footer levels do (Rule 128): one
135	// alphabet across the application, so a full gauge reads like a CRITICAL
136	// finding.
137	//
138	// It is a function rather than a package-level style because the thresholds
139	// are the whole of it; a var per level would leave the switch in the view,
140	// which is where Rule 125 says a colour must not be decided.
141	func LoadTextStyle(pct float64) lipgloss.Style {
142		base := lipgloss.NewStyle().Background(ColorBackground)
143		switch {
144		case pct >= LoadCriticalPercent:
145			return base.Foreground(ColorSeverityCritical).Bold(true)
146		case pct >= LoadWarnPercent:
147			return base.Foreground(ColorSeverityMedium)
148		default:
149			return base.Foreground(ColorOK)
150		}
151	}
152	
153	// TimingBarWidth is the width of a waterfall bar (§3.66), in cells — wider
154	// than GaugeWidth: a waterfall has several phases to tell apart on one line,
155	// where a gauge answers a single percentage, and the extra resolution is what
156	// keeps a phase as small as a handful of percent visible at all.
157	const TimingBarWidth = 24
158	
159	// TimingFillStyle is the colour a waterfall bar's filled cells take (§3.66) —
160	// reusing Gauge/GaugeFillWidth for the glyph and the rounding, but not
161	// LoadTextStyle for the colour: a phase taking most of a request's time is
162	// not a problem to spot, just a fact to read, so it gets one neutral colour
163	// rather than a severity gradient. ColorSecondary is what headers and active
164	// tabs already use for structural information, which is the same role here.
165	func TimingFillStyle() lipgloss.Style {
166		return lipgloss.NewStyle().Background(ColorBackground).Foreground(ColorSecondary)
167	}
168	
169	// GaugeTrackStyle is the colour a gauge's *empty* cells take — fixed,
170	// whatever the level, including a gauge that is entirely empty: the cell is
171	// still `░`, still coloured, never blank. It aliases ColorSeverityLow rather
172	// than DimStyle directly: DimStyle is this application's word for *absent*
173	// (a `-`, a zero, a placeholder), and an empty gauge cell is not absent — it
174	// is measured and low. ColorSeverityLow's own default now happens to be the
175	// same tone as ColorDim (a LOW finding reads as unremarkable as a "0" count,
176	// see colors.go) — the two coincide in colour without coinciding in name, so
177	// a theme separating "low severity" from "nothing found" moves the track
178	// with the former rather than the latter.
179	func GaugeTrackStyle() lipgloss.Style {
180		return lipgloss.NewStyle().Background(ColorBackground).Foreground(ColorSeverityLow)
181	}
